name: Portfolio Tracker
about: Everything a Meta Muse space needs to run Portfolio Tracker. The app is complete: the space is built only by copying these files as listed and connecting them. Nothing is designed, rewritten or added. Always read this file from the main branch: it describes the current version, and its steps work whatever version a space has now.

newSpace: Fetch every file named here fresh from the main branch of the repository. Never reuse a copy from an earlier conversation, an earlier version or another space.

Copy app.source byte for byte to app.copyTo and follow app.rules. The copy must then be exactly app.bytes bytes long (with the SHA-256 app.sha256, if you can compute one). If it isn't, fetch it once more. If it still isn't, keep the fetched file as it is and tell the user both sizes: never fix it by hand.
Copy each file in files to the place it gives, unchanged. Create each file in spaceOwnFiles from its template.
Connect only the imports that starterParts names to this space's starter, and remove what starterParts.remove names.
Create the tables in storage.tables as server/src/schema.ts defines them.
Set up exactly the server actions in actions, the network access in network and the scheduled job in cron. Ask the user to approve them, saying what each is for (approvals). Follow time.
Build the space. The files pass a strict TypeScript check as shipped: follow typescript if your build reports an error.
Run refreshMarketCache once. Dividend payment dates need nothing more (payouts.builtIn): don't do payouts.forMuse now, only when the user asks for it later.
Go through checks.newSpace and checks.always yourself, in the running space, then tell the user what finish says.
existingSpace: This updates or repairs a space made from any earlier version of this file, including one that was changed since it was made.
Fetch every file named here fresh from the main branch of the repository. Never reuse a copy from an earlier conversation, an earlier version or the space itself.

Keep the saved data: every row of every table in storage.tables, as it is. Never drop, clear, reset, re-create, migrate or reseed a table, and add no sample or test data. The app reads saved data from any earlier version and fills in what is new itself. If server/src/schema.ts has a table or column the space lacks, add it without touching existing rows.

Replace the app file and every file in files with the fresh copies, exactly as for a new space, including the app.bytes check. Never replace the files in spaceOwnFiles: they are this space's own (create one from its template only if it is missing).

Remove everything in the space's client and server code that this file doesn't list, except the starter's own modules that starterParts names and the files in spaceOwnFiles. That includes leftovers from earlier versions (such as embedded copies of the app/ folder, blob URLs, an import map, a boot ladder, a fetch cache, a patched or second copy of the app, or type-only edits made to an earlier copy of a file) and anything added around the app (a header, title bar, avatar, navigation labels, banner, tips, notes or restyling).

Make the server actions, network access and scheduled jobs exactly actions, network and cron: add what is missing, update what differs and remove what isn't listed. Ask the user to approve any new network access, saying what it is for (approvals). Follow time.
Build the space. The files pass a strict TypeScript check as shipped: follow typescript if your build reports an error.
Run refreshMarketCache once. Dividend payment dates need nothing more (payouts.builtIn): don't do payouts.forMuse now, only when the user asks for it later.
Go through checks.existingSpace and checks.always yourself, in the running space, then tell the user what finish says.

rules: byte for byte: never edit, rebuild, minify, split, unpack, restyle, translate or port it. bytes and sha256 above are the file's own; npm run build:app writes them
it is the whole front end, full screen; it mounts itself into #app and loads no other file

it never builds code from a string (no eval or Function()), so it passes the publishing check unchanged: never patch it. A check that finds a Function() in it (such as an ECharts custom-element check) is looking at an old copy: versions before 12 November 2026 had one. Fetch the file fresh from the main branch and confirm app.bytes. If a check objects to the current file anyway, leave it as it is and tell the user what the check said

it is tested at phone widths from 360px for controls that can't be reached and for content that scrolls sideways. If you find a defect, don't fix it in the space (in client/index.html, extra styles or a patched copy): the next update replaces those files and the defect comes back. Tell the user what you found, so it can be fixed in the repository

at start-up it keeps the space's style checker (__tunnel) for page elements only, so the chart library's own style objects keep their values and chart labels draw correctly: this is intended, leave it
nothing is added to the interface: no header, title bar, avatar, navigation labels, banner, tips or notes
no sample data: a new space starts empty

server/src/custom-payouts.ts.rule: this space's own, optional dividend-date connector (payouts.forMuse). Create it from the template when the space doesn't have it, unchanged; never replace, reset or remove it on an update

starterParts.client/src/api.ts: the starter's own server-action client; client/src/host.ts imports callAction(name, input) from it
starterParts.server/src/db.ts: the starter's own Drizzle database; server/src/actions.ts imports db from it
starterParts.remove: the starter's own App component, styles and #root: the page holds only #app

typescript: Every file here, and the custom-payouts.ts template, passes TypeScript's strict mode with noUncheckedIndexedAccess and the rest of a Bun project's default settings, as shipped (the repository's npm test checks this). If your build reports a type error in one of them, your copy is old: fetch it fresh from the main branch. If it still fails, change nothing about how the code works: make the smallest type-only change that builds (such as a non-null assertion), and tell the user the file, line and error, so it is fixed in the repository. The next update replaces that file again.

keys.app_state/portfolio: the whole app state as one JSON document
keys.market_cache/payouts:<SYMBOL>: each dividend's ex-date and payment date, from a built-in connector or the space's own

yahooGet.returns: parsed JSON body, also for non-200 answers

refreshMarketCache.returns: { ok, symbols, updated, failed, payouts, at }

getPayouts.input: { asks: [{ symbol, exchange?, currency?, name? }], force? }
getPayouts.returns: { ok, payouts: { [symbol]: { records, source, checkedAt, error? } } }
getPayouts.note: dividend payment dates from the built-in connectors (server/src/payouts.ts), then the space's own (server/src/custom-payouts.ts); the app calls it to check now

networkOwn: besides network: the hosts in CUSTOM_HOSTS of server/src/custom-payouts.ts, each approved by the user when the connector is written

approvals.query1.finance.yahoo.com: prices, dividends, splits and exchange rates (only ticker symbols are sent)
approvals.fc.yahoo.com: an anonymous Yahoo session for the payment dates of other US dividends, NYSE included (nothing of the user's is sent)
approvals.refreshMarketCache every 10 minutes: keeps prices and dividend dates fresh while the app is closed, so it opens at once

payouts.what: Each dividend's payment date, so the app adds a dividend to cash on the day the company pays it, and counts it as "to be paid" from its ex-date until then. Where no payment date is published, the app estimates it from the company's usual wait after the ex-date and shows it with a ~; a dividend never stays unpaid for ever.

builtIn.sgx: Singapore (.SI): shares, REITs and ETFs, full history, from SGX's own corporate actions
builtIn.nasdaq: US shares and ETFs listed on Nasdaq, full history, from Nasdaq
builtIn.yahoo: other US shares and ETFs, NYSE included: each latest dividend, kept as they build up, from Yahoo Finance
builtIn.asx: Australia (.AX): each latest dividend, kept as they build up, from the ASX
builtIn.setup: none: no sign-up, API key or login. refreshMarketCache looks each dividend-paying holding up once a day. Other listings (such as Hong Kong or London) get estimated dates, which is complete as it is

forMuse: Optional, and only when the user asks for it (Settings → Dividend Dates gives them the request to send you); never as part of setting up or updating the space.
It is for holdings whose payment dates are estimated because no built-in connector covers them (such as a Hong Kong, London, Tokyo or Bursa listing). getPayouts returns source null for them.

Find a free, public source of each one's dividend announcements that a server can read with no sign-up, API key or login: the exchange's own announcements first (such as HKEXnews for .HK or the London Stock Exchange's RNS for .L), otherwise the company's investor-relations dividend page.

Write customPayouts in server/src/custom-payouts.ts for exactly those holdings, following the rules at the top of that file. Return each dividend's ex-date and payment date as published, and never estimate a date yourself: payDate null when it isn't published (the app estimates it).
Put every host it reads in CUSTOM_HOSTS and ask the user to approve them as network access.
Call getPayouts with force: true for those holdings and check that each one now has records with payment dates.

If a source refuses a server (blocked, a login or a cookie challenge), try at most one other for that holding, then stop: tell the user its dates stay estimated and that they can type exact ones on the Dividends page.
Tell the user in plain words where each holding's dates now come from.

time: the app shows every time in the user's local time zone, taken from their device. Never set, force or convert a time zone anywhere in the space (never force UTC)
notNeeded: a database beyond the two tables
API keys, sign-ups or the user's own cookies
writing a dividend-date connector while setting up or updating

newSpace: Home shows 0.00 with an empty chart
adding "Buy AAPL, 10 shares" shows a value within a few seconds
reloading the space keeps the transaction
existingSpace: Home shows the saved portfolio with the same holdings and the same number of transactions as before the update; nothing was added to it
always: the Allocation page's donut labels (a ticker and its share, such as "AAPL: 100.0%") are plain text, with no box behind them
Home's "Last Updated" line shows the user's local time and time zone (such as GMT+8 in Singapore), never forced to UTC
Settings → Data & Backup → Where it is saved says "Muse space storage"
after refreshMarketCache has run once, a fresh device opens Home on the saved prices within a couple of seconds
Settings → Dividend Dates lists each dividend-paying holding with where its payment dates come from (SGX, Nasdaq, Yahoo Finance or ASX), or that they are estimated
on the Dividends page, each dividend sits on its own payment date: one whose date isn't published shows an estimated date with a ~, and none are piled up as "to be paid" on today

finish: Do every check yourself and report each one as passed, failed (with what you saw) or not possible here (and why). Don't leave a check for later.

Tell the user: the space is ready, the commit you copied from and the size of the app file you copied. For an update, also that their data is unchanged (the number of transactions and holdings, before and after).
Name anything that didn't go as this file says (a failed step, a type-only change and why, a check that failed), so it can be fixed in the repository. Change nothing else to work around it.

Then tell the user how to start: + adds a transaction, or Upload Files takes a CSV (Date, Action, Ticker, Shares, Price, Currency, Commission). Settings → Portfolio Settings sets the base currency and the dividend withholding tax. Settings → Dividend Dates shows where payment dates come from.
Ask nothing else of the user: the space needs no keys or accounts.
